title: Personal papershelf + quick synth: prompt-aware cache ideas
linked_artifacts: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.01234 (prompt-conditioned caching - hypothetical paper I skimmed)
content:
Purpose: quick, personal synth of a small reading set plus messy brainstorming of experiments to try on Redwood serving runtime. Not polished — this is for my sprint board and to share with Maya/Omar if useful.

Top-level takeaways (one-liners):
- Prompt-conditioned caching seems low-friction win: cache a small set of prefix embeddings/KV per prompt "type" rather than per user session.
- Heuristic prefix clustering (by token distribution + prompt template) can reduce cold-starts for chat apps with many short persistent contexts.
- Lightweight probing during early tokens (first 8-16) can choose between low-latency quantized kernel vs high-precision kernel.

Papers/blogs skimmed (note: quick reads, not full implementation):
1) "Prompt-conditioned KV caching" (arXiv skim)
   - Idea: detect prompt archetypes (instruction vs doc context vs code) and maintain small warm caches keyed by archetype.
   - Empirical: shows 20-30% token compute saving on some assistant workloads with negligible quality loss when archetype selection has >80% precision.
   - My note: interesting to combine with route-by-policy: hosted API can route archetype-matches to a warm pool.

2) "Adaptive kernel switching for low-latency inference" (conference talk notes)
   - Switching criteria: sequence length, cache hit probability, early-token perplexity estimate.
   - Latency win mainly for tail of short requests; risk: oscillation if classifier noisy.

3) Blog: "Sparse attention kernels and blocked-sparsity"
   - Takeaway: blocked patterns work well in practice for long context and are friendly to GEMM-level optimizations.

Quick synthesis: what seems new/underexplored for us
- Prompt-aware cache keys: use a tiny encoder to map prompt text -> cluster id. Keep per-cluster KV snapshots. Fast lookup + size-limited LRU.
- Cache combo: prefix cache (typical) + "soft-prefetch" where we pre-warm KV for high-traffic clusters during load spikes.
- Fallback policy: if cached KV causes >delta perplexity on a small heldout probe (5 tokens), we fall back to fresh compute.

Concrete experiment ideas (ranked):
A. Lightweight cluster encoder + per-cluster KV cache (2–4 week spike):
   - Build encoder (distil-BERT-ish, 1–3M params) to compute cluster hash for incoming prompt.
   - In serving runtime: maintain N small caches (N ~ 128), warm top-k clusters.
   - Metrics: token compute saved, latency p50/p95, small eval set quality delta (ROUGE/LLM-specific metric).
   - Safety: add conservative fallback if cached KV diverges (use probe tokens).

B. Early-token probe classifier for kernel selection (1–2 week spike):
   - Collect dataset: pairs (first 8 tokens, best kernel choice for latency/quality). Train cheap MLP.
   - Integrate into request pre-stage: pick quantized vs full precision kernel + whether to allocate extra threads.

C. Simulated A/B in hosted API: route subset of requests to warm-pool vs baseline. Measure cost and customer-visible latency.

Data/Instrumentation needed: (notes to self and infra asks)
- Need token-level timing traces for first 32 tokens, plus model-level cache hit metadata.
- Small annotation set: label ~1k prompts with archetype and acceptable quality thresholds.
- Hook to Console dashboards: per-cluster hit rates, per-cluster latency, quality regressions.

Risks / open questions:
- Privacy/regulatory: per-cluster caches might accidentally group PII-heavy prompts. We need to ensure caches are not storing raw PII blobs and tie into KMS policy.
- Cold clusters explosion: how to limit number of clusters? Use frequency-based eviction and approximate LSH to bucket.
- Metric noise: perplexity-based probe may not correlate with downstream task metrics. We need small task-aligned eval sets.

Short checklist / TODOs:
- [ ] Prototype a tiny cluster encoder and run offline clustering on 50k recent assistant prompts (ask Data infra for sample).
- [ ] Wire a toy per-cluster KV cache in local runtime (single-GPU), measure hit rates and compute savings.
- [ ] Run small internal A/B to measure degredation (if any) on hallucination-prone prompts.
- [ ] Discuss privacy constraints with Security before any persistent cache across customers.

Notes for conversation with Maya (sync on 2026-07-02):
- Show short demo: how cluster encoder groups typical prompts (few-shot, chat history, long doc context).
- Ask Omar about feasibility of probe classifier in pre-stage without adding >1ms median latency.

Random fragments / brainstorm:
- Could we store "delta-KV" snapshots that only keep important head activations for tokens that changed from cached state? Smaller memory footprint.
- For private deployments: make caches opt-in per customer and expose cache control in customer config.
- Idea: expose cache-hit hints in API response headers to let clients adapt (e.g., client can decide to re-send updated context if it's a miss).

References / quick links I kept in browser: (copied for followup)
- arXiv prompt-conditioned caching (see linked_artifacts)
- Redwood internal: github.com/redwood-inference/example-prefix-cache
- MLSys 2026 talk deck (linked_artifacts)

Closing: keep this as a working doc. Will refine into a short PRD if prototype shows >10% token-cost savings with <1% quality regression on our evals.

-- Ethan
